questions.question_text: The vectors $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}x\\-5\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}$ satisfy $\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}=1$. Find the value of $x$.

options.why: Solved $4x=-16$ instead of $4x=16$ after moving the $-15$ across.
Stopped at $4x=16$ without dividing by $4$.
Added $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{c}$ instead of subtracting it, giving $-6+8$.
Forgot to double $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}$, giving $-3-8$.
Doubled both terms, giving $-6-16$; the $2$ multiplies only $\underset{\sim}{b}$.

questions.question_text: The vectors $\begin{pmatrix}x\\1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}x-3\\6\end{pmatrix}$ have a dot product of $10$. Find the possible values of $x$.

options.why: Sign slip when factorising $x^{2}-3x-4$, giving $(x+4)(x-1)$.
Wrote the second product as $6x$ instead of $6$, solving $x^{2}+3x-10=0$.
Gave only one root; a quadratic equation here has two valid solutions.
